notes: Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001): with skill 91%, without 82% (+9 points). Gains are concentrated in the README (+14) and the review (+22). There's no gain on the how-to (82% both) or release notes (88% both).

Haiku keeps making some mistakes even with the skill: it invents doc URLs (2 of 3 how-tos with the skill, 1 of 3 without), lists internal refactor and CI changes in release notes (2/3 with, 3/3 without), and uses 'Option A/B' or headed steps instead of an ordered list with 'If …' steps (2/3 with, 3/3 without). The skill's guidance reaches Haiku less reliably.
Cost: +28% tokens (about 40k against 31k per run). Haiku with the skill still uses fewer tokens than Sonnet or Opus without it.

Same 4 evals, test project (Python 3.14), check script and Opus 5.5 blind graders as Opus's iteration 2, so the three models are directly comparable. Sonnet and Haiku runs were pooled and shuffled together for grading. One with-skill review response still names the TGDP guide files it read, which is part of its genuine output.
Prompts also told each run to keep temporary files in its own folder, a change from iteration 2 made after the iteration-3 scratchpad collision. Otherwise identical.
Wall-clock time is unreliable across waves: a usage-limit interruption meant some runs were re-done later under different load. Compare token counts rather than seconds.
